'''Ashkan Nikeghbali Cisakht<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=204872662 |url=https://viaf.org/viaf/204872662/ |access-date=2023-02-13 |website=viaf.org}}</ref>''' ({{langx|fa|اشکان نیک‌اقبالی}}; born {{cn-span|text=September 15,|date=February 2023|reason=date not mentioned in source}} 1975<ref name=":0" />) is a {{Cn-span|text=French|date=February 2023|reason=nationality not mentioned in source}} mathematician and university professor {{Cn-span|text=of Iranian descent|date=February 2023|reason=ethnicity not mentioned at source}}. He holds the chair of Financial Mathematics at the [[University of Zurich]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=University of Zurich - Person |url=https://math.uzh.ch/index.php?id=people&id=people&key1=1833&L=1 |access-date=2023-02-13 |website=math.uzh.ch |language=en}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Nikeghbali obtained his PhD at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in 2005 with the thesis "Temps aléatoires, filtrations et sous-martingales: quelques développements récents", supervised by [[Marc Yor]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Ashkan Nikeghbali - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=110687 |access-date=2023-02-13 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> Prior to that, he was a researcher from February 2004 to July 2004 at the [[Isaac Newton Institute]] on the topic of "Random matrix approaches in number theory."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nikeghbali |title=Random matrix approaches in number theory |date=25 February 2021 |url=https://www.newton.ac.uk/event/rma/ |access-date=12 February 2023}}</ref> After completing his PhD, Nikeghbali first worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[American Institute of Mathematics]] (under the direction of Brian Conrey) at [[University of Rochester]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=Archived copy | url=https://www.math.uzh.ch/en/fileadmin/user/ashkan/publikation/0505623..pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240815223556/https://www.math.uzh.ch/en/fileadmin/user/ashkan/publikation/0505623..pdf | archive-date=2024-08-15}}</ref> In June 2006, he was appointed Heinz-Hopf Lecturer at [[ETH Zurich]]. In March 2007, Nikeghbali was appointed assistant professor at the Institute of Mathematics at the [[University of Zurich]]. He was promoted to Extraordinary Professor of Applied Mathematics there in 2009.{{cn|date=February 2023}}

== Research ==
Nikeghbali's research focuses on [[financial mathematics]], [[probability theory]], and [[analytic number theory]].<ref name=":1" /> In particular, he works in the areas of [[portfolio theory]], [[stochastic processes]], [[random operator]]s and [[Random matrix|matrices]], and the application of stochastics in number theory and combinatorics.{{cn|date=February 2023}}

In [[asymptotic probability theory]], Nikeghbali, together with Féray, Méliot, and Kowalski introduced the concept of [[Mod-Ф convergence]]. In number theory, he, together with Chhaibi and Najnudel, introduced the concept of [[stochastic zeta function]].{{cn|date=February 2023}}

Nikeghbali supervised at least six PhD students during his time at the University of Zurich.<ref name=":2" />

== Other activities ==
Member of the [[world.minds]] community since 2008.{{cn|date=February 2023}} Member of the Scientific Advisory Board of [[swissQuant]].<ref name=":1" /> Member of the advisory board of [[EVMTech]].<ref name=":1" /> Strategy advisor for data analysis and modeling of stochastic processes at [[Roche Holding]] in Basel.{{cn|date=February 2023}}

== Awards ==
Honorary doctorate from the [[University of Alba Iulia]] in Romania.<ref name=":1" />
